Messages.Author: Drain
Messages.Body:
Name: Deep-seeded Infiltration
Cardtype:
Cost: 2 blood
Only usable after successfully bleeding your prey for 2 or more.
Your prey reveals his hand to you.
Put this card on this vampire, the vampire with this card gets +2 bleed while bleeding your prey. Burn this card if this minion is blocked by a minion controlled by your prey. A vampire may only have one Deep-seeded Infiltration.

Game development:
- Increase the viability of the City !Gangrel through leverage of their clan disciplines.

Flavor:
- Obfuscate & Protean both possibilitate the impersonation of a third party (Mask of 1K faces, Old Friends, Loki's Gift) so how effective can we assume that a junction of the two would be at the same task? Pretty darn effective, if you asked me.

Balance:
- Ousting power is the challenge that this card aims to tackle. I didn't want it to be too easy to play so I drew heavily from Enkil Cog and made it only be playable in the case of a successful bleed on the prey. Much like Enkil, it is also a modifier and not an action since the !Gangrel don't multiact much and need card efficiency.

- Enkidu and other big'ol'meanies never left my mind while designing the card, so I made the restriction that if you're blocked by your prey the card goes away, conversely the bleed needing to be for two is a tricky restriction to impose on the !Gangrel... but once again it is aimed at making this card less playable by Enkidu. I'm not too sure if it should be dropped to increase the general playability of the card or not.

- The +2 bleed only works on the prey because it seemed thematically correct for the minion to only receive bleed while attacking the infiltrated Meth.

Competitiveness:
- High. Ousting power where there was little to none, enough said.

Drain

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
Personally, I like the overall idea - dual-discipline aggression for the !Gangrel (and other lucky enough vampires) - but I'm not sure that, for me, it captures what I'd like the !Gangrel to do.

This way, it sort of encourages going for a fairly routine stealth-bleed deck - lots of Obf stealth, lots of Pro stealth (choose according to your needs/disciplines/blood costs), maybe a bunch of bleed cards (Hacks, Phones). Possibly go Anarch and play Skullduggery - although it's mostly the ability to flex between stealth and bleed that makes that card interesting to me, but maybe you'd try it, and you could also use Monkey Wrench if you were a !Gangrel Anarch, maybe. Spying Mission would help a little with bounce (responsible stealth-bleed). You could probably include a few combat surprises for would-be rushers, whether that's the odd claw or the odd Earth Meld.

And with the exception of the odd aggressive combat option, it kinda feels like more or less every other stealth-bleed deck going - lots of stealth, some bleed, maybe some combat defence. And even there, the Dementation Malkavians can throw out the odd Coma, the Lasombra can Arms of the Abyss + Disarm, that kind of thing.

What would feel more flavoursome but - and these are the important words - probably be a damn sight less playable would be something like:

[OBF][PRO] Play at the end of combat when this vampire ir still ready and the opponent is not. Put this card on this vampire. This vampire has...

... and then go with the +1 bleed, +1 bleed if no ready vampires option.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> jamesatzephyr wrote:
> and you could also use Monkey Wrench if you were a !Gangrel Anarch, maybe.
>
And indeed it's the fact that you can play it that make it precious, more than the number you actually play. Monkey wrench is a watered-down Walk of caine, and a methuselah with 10 or 12 blood could be in killing range if you have high-blood anarchs.

The main problem with Monkey wrench is that you usually can't have horde of weenie anarch (even if in the lore it's a lot more likely than Serena the white anarch ...), and keeping so much blood is pretty hard, especially with smallish !gangrel.

Maybe a card that replicate the high-cost, high-bleed capacity of Walk of caine could be what !Gangrel are lacking ?

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ohlmann wrote:
> Maybe a card that replicate the high-cost, high-bleed capacity of Walk of caine could be what !Gangrel are lacking ?
>
It might give you an opportunity to explore the 'pack' elements that were suggested for the !Gangrel. e.g. burning blood off other !Gangrel you control, tapping other !Gangrel you control, having some effect that's capped based on the number of !Gangrel you control.

Somewhere between Walk of Caine and Ensemble, perhaps.

Messages.Author: Drain

I find it curious that everyone thinks the City !Gangrel need help with ousting power but no one seems to quite agree on how best to do it.

Drain

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
That's because we want something with distinctive gameplay, flavorful feel, and/or that won't be exploited by an already strong deck. It's far from easy.

Also, not everybody have the same opinion on the !gangrel. Some think they are heavy diabolist, other think they are mainly pack animals, some other yet think they are natural killer, with some amount of overlap between the opinion. Something that help create the feel of a lion pack is naturally different from something that create the geel of a lone tiger.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Ohlmann wrote:
> Also, not everybody have the same opinion on the !gangrel. Some think they are heavy diabolist, other think they are mainly pack animals, some other yet think they are natural killer, with some amount of overlap between the opinion.
>
In particular, in V:TES terms, they don't have a niche, or an edge in one particualr area. Not that it would necessarily be a strong strategy (now) - but nothing leaps out at you and says, in V:TES, "here's something I can do - even if it's a bit rubbish".

When you do have something like that, it tends to focus opinion a little bit more. For example, melee weapon combat isn't all that great, but it's a bit of a !Salubri signature so you often see suggestions in that area.

The City Gangrel, they have a somewhat ineffectual combat angle - aggro=poke combined with little damage, little blood gain, and Psyche! (one of the weaker anti-S:CE cards). Lots of stealth with little bleed. No real wall capabilities. No particularly significant political angle. Pool gain is moderately tricky. They have a few possible breeders (although a quick search says they're in group 3-4 only, really), but blood gain is slightly trickier. Multi-acting is hard - Dual Form inferior isn't totally unplayable, but it's expensive (it's that blood gain again), and it's up-front - it yells 'block me, jam my hand' to a player that cares about that, whereas Freak Drive is opportunistic and can come after.

Maybe multi-acting would be an option.
